subject: Velocity SLA checks + multi-geo data path clarifications
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finexa.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Thanks for the demo today — good discussion. A few clarifying items we need to capture so our infra team can greenlight pilot procurement: 

1) Latency targets: we need P95 round-trip (client->redwood->client) guidance for streaming and non-streaming APIs by region. Rough target we care about: US (primary), EU (cross-border tolerance), APAC (higher tolerance). Can you confirm typical P95 numbers and the conditions (seq length, model family) you measured?

2) Throughput & concurrency: our main workload is low-latency interactive chat but with occasional bursts (conference support) — baseline 200 rps, burst to 1,200 concurrent simultaneous users; what concurrency model do you recommend?

3) Cold-start & KV cache warmup: for our conversational agents we expect lots of short-lived convs; what cold-start overhead and cache-warmup guidance do you have?

4) Data residency: EU GDPR requirement — user content for EU customers must remain in EU for storage and logs. Can you outline options for routing, metrics, and audit logs to meet this?

5) Test window: we'd like a 48-hour canary in EU and US to validate latencies under production traffic. What do you need from us to set this up?

Attached is a short perf matrix we use internally — will share sample traffic as a follow-up.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Senior Product Manager — Finexa
liam.oconnor@finexa.com

Attachments: perf_matrix_v2.csv (spreadsheet with seq length distribution)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finexa.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 13:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Liam — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers inline below, plus next steps so we don't lose momentum.

1) Latency (P95, client-visible) — ballpark numbers we expect on our hosted offering for a t5-ish open model family at moderate sequence lengths (prompt ~120 tokens, response ~60 tokens):
   - US (regional): ~110–180 ms
   - EU (regional): ~140–260 ms (cross-region + misc routing can add variance)
   - APAC: ~240–380 ms (depending on final region presence; Tokyo <-> Singapore varies)
   For streaming APIs (SSE), per-chunk latency is similar but end-to-end time increases due to tokenization and streaming chunk sizing. We'll attach a short playbook that notes measurement windows and sample seq lengths.

2) Throughput & concurrency — recommended config:
   - Baseline: reserve 2 dedicated workers (each worker sustained ~100–150 rps depending on model and quantization)
   - Burst handling: enable autoscaling with burst pool; we can absorb brief spikes up to ~1,200 concurrent active connections by spinning up burst nodes (requires burst capacity reservation).
   - Continuous batching helps throughput but can add a few ms to p95; we'll tune the batching policy for interactive workloads.

3) Cold-start & KV cache warmup — expectations:
   - Cold start (new model instance): ~600–1,200 ms for first token depending on model size and hardware.
   - KV cache warmup for conv continuity: after a session's first few tokens, subsequent responses drop to the P95 numbers above. We recommend sticky routing for session affinity for best results.

4) Data residency options:
   - Hosted: we can guarantee regional routing and store EU customer content and logs in EU-only buckets/tenants (requires SOC2+ addendum for audit trail).
   - Dedicated/Private: full EU-only deployment (VPC + KMS) if you need certifiable residency.
   - Metrics & traces: we can either push anonymized metrics to your EU tenant or provide an on-prem metrics collector.

5) Test window — what we need from you:
   - Representative traffic file (you mentioned you have one)
   - A short list of critical endpoints and expected sequence-length distribution (attach to ticket)
   - A preferred dates window and success criteria (p95 thresholds by region)

Next steps (action items):
   - Vanessa: provision 48-hour canary environments in US + EU, enable token-level latency tracing, attach perf matrix to the ticket. (ETA: 2 business days)
   - Marissa: prepare SLO playbook and SLA/penalty language we can show procurement.
   - Liam: share the traffic sample and confirm preferred window.

I've attached the SLO playbook (slo_playbook.pdf) and will follow up with a single ticket that captures the test config. If EU residency needs are strict, we should plan a short private pilot.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference | https://www.redwoodinference.com

Attachments: slo_playbook.pdf
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finexa.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jul 2027 19:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Looping in a few infra specifics and a proposed test config. Quoting Vanessa below for context: 

> 1) Latency (P95, client-visible) — ballpark numbers we expect...

A few clarifications from the runtime side: 
- Model & seq assumptions: the numbers Vanessa gave assume a 7B-ish quantized open model and typical prompt/response sizes. If Finexa plans to use a 70B dense model, expect +30–70% on p95 and ~2–3x on resource cost.
- Streaming: use chunked responses with 64-token chunks for best perceived latency; smaller chunks increase overhead. For chat UIs, set initial chunk to 16–32 tokens to improve TTF (time to first token).
- Concurrency model: we recommend per-session affinity TTL of 15 minutes. For conference bursts, use a dedicated burst pool with pre-warmed instances (pre-warm reduces cold starts to sub-200ms on first token).
- Routing: to satisfy EU residency for logs, we'll route inference traffic through EU gateways and store logs in EU-only buckets. Application metadata (non-content) can be aggregated in US if acceptable, but we'll mark anything customer-content as EU-only.

Proposed 48-hour canary config (what we'll provision):
- EU: 2 pre-warmed GPU nodes (gpu-rt-type), autoscale + 2 burst nodes, token-level tracing on.
- US: 3 pre-warmed GPU nodes, autoscale + 3 burst nodes.
- Logging: EU bucket with 30-day retention for trial.
- Success criteria: P95 <= 220ms EU, <= 170ms US under the sample traffic; no data leaving EU buckets for EU test traffic.

One ask to Finexa: provide a short-lived service account key for us to push metrics to your EU bucket, and a sample of the production traffic (anonymized) so we can simulate realistic concurrency spikes.

I'll add these details to the ticket Vanessa is creating.

—Diego Fernandez
Senior Performance Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finexa.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2027 09:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's perf discovery call

Thanks — this is exactly what we needed. Quick confirmations: 

- We'll start with the 7B open model family for the canary.
- I'll share a sanitized traffic sample and a short doc with our success criteria by EOD.
- Procurement copied here (procurement@finexa.com) — can you share the SLO language and an estimate for the 48-hour pilot (cost table for burst capacity)? We need this to get PO approval.

Proposed pilot dates: Jul 14–16 (EU window overlapping a US late-night period) — does that work on your side?

Also: can you confirm whether audit logs for EU-chat sessions will contain full user content or only pointers (we need full content to troubleshoot but prefer a retention policy that satisfies GDPR).

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Liam
Senior Product Manager — Finexa
